findings.message: SPEC §4.9.3 core/history-entry at L4: every non-merge commit in range adds one entry. This test commits test(app): cover a with no HISTORY entry and asserts the range yields no core/history-entry finding, so it pins behaviour the SPEC forbids. Either each commit in the fixture adds its own entry (title: a range whose every commit carries its entry passes), or a SPEC change must first relax L4 to one entry per range.

Any docs/HISTORY/ path in scope now exempts the whole scope, so at L4 a range with one entry and N commits passes core/history-entry, contrary to §4.9.3 (one entry per non-merge commit in range; EC-9 says L4 blocks a commit that bypassed L3). The comment defers counting to staged-history and history-entry-complete, but no test in this change proves an L4 per-commit count fires for a range short of entries; add that missing-entry-commit case or judge per commit.

Presence of a HISTORY path is not an added entry: a code change that only edits an old HISTORY file (or a whitespace touch on one) now passes core/history-entry. core/history-append-only may block edits in place but not a pure append-free touch; the exemption should key on an added entry, not on the path.
The regression and unit test entries name the same test (same path and title); list it once or name a distinct unit test.
